subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Sidewalk Terrace Tradition
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Sidewalk Terrace Tradition.

hook.text: Parisian café chairs face the street. You don't look at your companion—you watch the city together.

buildup.text: The terrasse (sidewalk seating) was legalized in 1856. It transformed cafés from indoor rooms into urban theaters.

discovery.text: Impressionist painters loved terrasses. Renoir and Manet painted café scenes that defined Parisian visual culture.

twist.text: Terrasse seats cost more than indoor ones—you're paying for the privilege of seeing and being seen by Paris.

climax.text: The café terrasse became synonymous with French lifestyle. It's protected by cultural regulation to this day.

punchline.text: Face the street, sip slowly, watch the world. Paris in a chair.

quiz.question: Why do Parisian café chairs traditionally face the street?
options: So patrons watch the city—the café is an urban theater
